Let \(I_d\) denote the \(d\times d\) identity matrix. For \(\beta=(\beta_0,\beta_1,\beta_2,\beta_3)\in\mathbb R^4\), define
\[
O(\beta)=\begin{pmatrix}
\beta_0&-\beta_1&-\beta_2&-\beta_3\\
\beta_1&\beta_0&-\beta_3&\beta_2\\
\beta_2&\beta_3&\beta_0&-\beta_1\\
\beta_3&-\beta_2&\beta_1&\beta_0
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Set \(O_1=O(1,0,0,0)\), \(O_2=O(0,1,0,0)\), \(O_3=O(0,0,1,0)\), \(O_4=O(0,0,0,-1)\), and
\[
P=\frac12\begin{pmatrix}I_4&O_1\\I_4&O_2\\I_4&O_3\\I_4&O_4\end{pmatrix},\qquad
D=\operatorname{diag}\!\left(I_4,\frac12I_4,\frac13I_4,\frac14I_4\right),\qquad S=P^\top P.
\]
The matrix \(S\) is invertible. Let \(e_1,e_5\) be the first and fifth standard coordinate vectors of \(\mathbb R^8\), and define the mean gradients
\[
\xi=\begin{pmatrix}(PS^{-1}e_1)^\top\\0_{1\times16}\end{pmatrix},\qquad
\eta=\begin{pmatrix}(PS^{-1}e_5)^\top\\0_{1\times16}\end{pmatrix}.
\]

Work on the periodic cell \(Y=(0,2\pi)^2\). Define
\[
t(x,y)=\frac12+\frac{\cos x+\cos y+\cos(x+3y)}6.
\]
For each integer \(N\ge2\), put \(h=2\pi/N\) and define a two-phase indicator by
\[
\chi_N(x,y)=\mathbf1_{\{(y-kh)/h<t(x,kh)\}}\qquad\text{when }kh\le y<(k+1)h,\quad k=0,\ldots,N-1,
\]
extended periodically in both variables; \(\mathbf1\) equals one when its condition holds and zero otherwise.

For \(0<\rho<1/3\), these indicators specify two constituent tensors whose horizontal blocks are \(I_{16}\) and \(I_{16}-\rho PP^\top\), respectively, and whose common vertical block is \(D\). For \(F\in\mathbb R^{2\times16}\), let \(F_x,F_y\in\mathbb R^{16}\) be the transposes of its first and second rows. Define the effective energy
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal E_{\rho,N}(F)=\min_{v\in H^1_{\mathrm{per}}(Y;\mathbb R^{16})}\frac1{(2\pi)^2}\int_Y
&\bigl(F_x+\partial_xv\bigr)^\top
 \bigl(I_{16}-\rho\chi_N PP^\top\bigr)
 \bigl(F_x+\partial_xv\bigr)\\
&+\bigl(F_y+\partial_yv\bigr)^\top D\bigl(F_y+\partial_yv\bigr)\,dx\,dy.
\end{aligned}
\]
Here \(H^1_{\mathrm{per}}\) consists of \(2\pi\)-periodic functions with square-integrable values and first weak derivatives. No factor \(1/2\) is included in the energy.

Determine the unique ordered pair \((p,c)\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\times(\mathbb R\setminus\{0\})\) such that
\[
\lim_{N\to\infty}\bigl(\mathcal E_{\rho,N}(\eta)-\mathcal E_{\rho,N}(\xi)\bigr)
=c\,\rho^p+O(\rho^{p+1})\qquad(\rho\downarrow0).
\]
The limit in \(N\) is taken first, at each fixed positive \(\rho\). Give \(c\) exactly.
</problem>

38	Here is a direct justification, including why the rapidly varying indicators can be replaced by \(t\) in this problem. Set

50	\qquad \|t_N-t\|_\infty\le Ch.                       \tag{2}

52	For every smooth periodic vector field \(g\) and every periodic \(w\in H^1\), integration by parts gives
53	\[

55	\int_Y(\chi_N-t)g\cdot w_x
56	={}&-\int_YR_Ng_y\cdot w_x

108	\[
109	a+b=(I-\rho Kt)^{-1}a.
110	\]

112	\[
113	\mathcal E_\rho(F)
114	=|f|^2-\rho\left\langle a,t(I-\rho Kt)^{-1}a\right\rangle.

124	### The matrix identity responsible for the cancellations
125

127	\[
128	w_i(q)=\frac{im^2}{4(im^2+n^2)},\qquad i=1,2,3,4,  \tag{8}

131	\[
132	K(q)=
133	\begin{pmatrix}
134	\alpha(q)I_4&C(q)\\
135	C(q)^\top&\alpha(q)I_4
136	\end{pmatrix},

138	\alpha(q)=\sum_{i=1}^4w_i(q),\quad
139	C(q)=\sum_{i=1}^4w_i(q)O_i.                         \tag{9}
140	\]

143	\[
144	\Delta(K_1\cdots K_\ell)
145	=e_5^\top K_1\cdots K_\ell e_5
146	-e_1^\top K_1\cdots K_\ell e_1.
147	\]

150	\Delta(K_1\cdots K_\ell)=0\quad (0\le\ell\le3),     \tag{10}

161	\]

163	\[

165	-(C_1C_2^\top C_3C_4^\top)_{11}
166	=-2\det(w_{ji}),
167	\]

188	\[

190	\]

199	\Delta\bigl(K(q_1)K(q_2)K(q_3)K(q_4)\bigr).         \tag{12}
200	\]
201	
202	We now identify every path that can contribute.
203	
204	Let \(n_a,n_b,n_c\) be the net numbers of the three positive modes. Closure gives
205	\[
206	n_a+n_c=0,\qquad n_b+3n_c=0.
207	\]
208	If \(n_c\ne0\), the number of nonzero steps is at least
209	\[
210	|n_a|+|n_b|+|n_c|=5|n_c|.
211	\]
212	Therefore the five steps must be precisely
213	\[
214	\{c,-a,-b,-b,-b\},
215	\]
216	or their negatives.
217	
218	If \(n_c=0\), all three net numbers vanish. There are then an even number of nonzero steps, so at least one of the five steps is zero. 220	Finally, for the multiset \(\{c,-a,-b,-b,-b\}\), the first and last steps must be \(c,-a\) in some order: otherwise \(q_1\) or \(q_4=-s_5\) has zero horizontal component, making its multiplier zero. This leaves exactly two paths, and their negatives give two more.
221	
222	For the path
223	\[
224	(c,-b,-b,-b,-a),
225	\]
226	the intermediate modes are
227	\[
228	(1,3),(1,2),(1,1),(1,0).
229	\]
230	Their weight matrix is
231	\[
232	W=
233	\begin{pmatrix}
234	1/40&1/22&1/16&1/13\\
235	1/20&1/12&3/28&1/8\\
236	1/8&1/6&3/16&1/5\\
237	1/4&1/4&1/4&1/4
238	\end{pmatrix},
239	\qquad
240	\det W=\frac3{51251200}.                            \tag{13}
241	\]
242	The other three paths either negate all the modes or reverse the four rows. Neither operation changes the determinant.
243	
244	Combining (11)–(13), the coefficient is therefore
245	\[
246	c=-4\left(\frac1{12}\right)^5(-2\det W)
247	=\frac{8}{12^5}\frac3{51251200}
248	=\boxed{\frac1{531372441600}}.                      \tag{14}
249	\]
250	
251	Since this number is positive and nonzero, (4) and the convergent expansion prove
252	\[
253	\lim_{N\to\infty}
254	\bigl(\mathcal E_{\rho,N}(\eta)-\mathcal E_{\rho,N}(\xi)\bigr)
255	=\frac{\rho^5}{531372441600}+O(\rho^6).
256	\]
